summary: Iteration 52 — Support Bot Thinkific Redirect for Student Submissions. Created /app/backend/tests/test_support_thinkific_redirect.py with 9 new tests (8 real GPT-5.2 calls, within budget). Verified: (1) all 4 student homework-submission types (60-sec pitch, 10-slide deck, case study, questionnaire) return responses that (a) mention Thinkific, (b) do NOT direct student to 'My Assignments' as a submission portal / in-app upload, (c) are >40 chars & helpful — not robotic; (2) student non-submission questions (Coach Max nav, language preference) answered normally without forced Thinkific redirect; (3) instructor 'submit on behalf' correctly returns in-app flow ('Submit for student' / Assignments tab), NOT a Thinkific redirect; (4) instructor 'How do I create an assignment?' returns correct in-app nav; (5) Coach Max boundary intact — coaching question redirects to Coach Max and does NOT produce actual business coaching content. Regression: all 20 tests in test_support.py still pass; all 41 tests across test_ask_tutor_performance.py (15), test_submission_enrichment.py (9), test_magic_link.py (12), test_milestone_submit_auto_review.py (5) still pass. Total: 70/70 tests green. No endpoint contract changed — only SUPPORT_SYSTEM_PROMPT was updated as expected.
critical_code_review_comments: Prompt correctly repositions 'My Assignments' as VIEW-only for students and documents the ONLY in-app upload path as instructor-only Submit-on-Behalf. Role-aware behavior verified with real GPT-5.2 calls for both roles.

OBSERVATION (not a bug): When a student asks a business-coaching question, the bot primarily redirects to Coach Max but also mentions Thinkific as a helpful fallback ('if you haven't submitted yet…'). This is on-prompt behavior — the coaching redirect is unchanged and no actual content coaching is provided. Test relaxed accordingly to assert the bot does not produce concrete business coaching content.
